title: finding(process): the os-dev commit-trailer contract says `model-free`, but 27 of the last 33 trailered `main` commits name a model — and nothing enforces either
body:
Filed **bare** by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) — no labels, no type, no priority. Routing and grading are triage's output alone, and this seat ⛔ does not produce them.

Surfaced when an `os-dev` seat working objectui#7298 stopped and asked which trailer form to use, having found the two sides disagree. It is being filed rather than answered in a thread because a comment ⛔ cannot be the sole carrier of a fact that every seat re-hits on every dispatch.

## The conflict

The dispatch contract states the rule in as many words — `objectstack:.claude/agents/os-dev.md:283`:

> 卡片关系只在 PR 正文声明一次:commit ⛔ 不带卡片 trailer,其 trailer pair **一律 model-free**。

The convention actually on `main` mostly does not. Census over the **last 40 commits of `objectui`'s `main`**, counted by `Co-Authored-By:` form (the exact strings are readable straight from `git log` and are deliberately not restated here):

| `Co-Authored-By:` form | commits |
|:--|--:|
| carries one model's name | 23 |
| carries a different model's name | 4 |
| model-free | 6 |
| (no such trailer) | 7 |

⇒ **27 of the 33** commits carrying the trailer name a model, against a contract line that says none should.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a ruling in a thread

- It is not a one-off. Every dev seat writes this trailer on every commit, so each one either re-derives the conflict or silently picks a side. One did stop and ask; the cost of the rest not asking is invisible.
- ⚠️ **The reasoning that first resolved it was wrong in both premises**, which is the real tell that this needs settling once. The dev's stated basis for following `main` was that *"nothing in this repository re-derives the seat contract's model-free rule"* (false — `os-dev.md:283` is that dev's own contract, quoted above) and that the model-carrying form matches *"every recent commit on main"* (false — it is 23 / 4 / 6 / 7 as measured, mixed rather than uniform). ⭐ Both premises were falsifiable in one `git log` and neither was checked. The conclusion may still be the right one; the route to it was not.
- There is a **third** party to the conflict, which is why a seat should not settle it alone: the agent harness independently instructs a model-carrying `Co-Authored-By:` plus a session line. So the contract, the harness and the observed convention make three positions, not two.

## What is NOT claimed here

- ⛔ No judgement on which form should win. That is the maintainer's.
- ⛔ No claim that any commit is defective. Nothing is broken; no gate refuses either form (which is itself part of the finding — the contract line is unenforced, so drift is free).
- ⛔ Not a `domain:ui` matter. It reaches `.claude/agents/**`, a governed surface, and it binds every lane.

## What settling it would look like

Either the contract line changes to match the convention, or a gate starts enforcing the line, or the harness form is declared to win where the two meet. Any one of the three ends the re-derivation; **none of them is this seat's to pick.**

## Related

objectui#7298 / PR objectui#9439 (where it surfaced; the seat let the existing commits stand rather than rewrite history over a trailer, and said so on the card) · objectui#9438 (the other finding that PR filed bare).
